repo_notes.content: SCOPE — what this repository is and is not. swift-pjsip-gen is a code generator, not a SIP stack. Its SwiftPM plugins parse the PJSIP C headers a consumer actually builds against — the headers shipped inside the swift-pjsip xcframework — and emit the Swift ergonomics the C importer does not provide: today @retroactive CustomStringConvertible and CustomDebugStringConvertible conformances for PJSIP's config structs and enums, discovered transitively from named roots. It contains no PJSIP code and links nothing from PJSIP; it reads headers as text. Do not generate pages documenting pjsua, pjmedia or any other PJSIP API — the types this package emits conformances for belong to swift-pjsip. One structural oddity is deliberate and must not be described as duplication awaiting cleanup: CHeaderParser.swift, Config.swift and TypeDiscoverer.swift exist as byte-identical copies in both Sources/PJSIPSwiftGenCore/ and Plugins/PJSIPSwiftGenPlugin/, because the build-tool plugin cannot rely on its executable tool having been built when createBuildCommands runs under Xcode, where SwiftPM pre-builds plugin tools and Xcode defers them. scripts/check-duplicate-sources.sh fails the build the moment the copies drift, Sources/PJSIPSwiftGenCore/ is the canonical copy, and docs/DESIGN.md records the diagnosis together with an open question about whether the duplication is truly forced.
repo_notes.author: maintainer

repo_notes.content: AUTHORITATIVE SOURCES, in precedence order. docs/DESIGN.md is the canonical record of why this package is shaped the way it is: it documents the SwiftPM and Xcode plugin constraints that were hit and worked around, the three-way resolution order used to locate the PJSIP headers, the choices that look odd from outside, and the open questions that remain — including which workarounds might be droppable if a constraint turns out not to hold. It supersedes any inference drawn from the file tree. README.md is the consumer-facing entry point and carries the product table and the pjsip-swift-gen.json configuration format. Sources/PJSIPSwiftGenCore/Documentation.docc/ holds the DocC catalogue for the core library.
repo_notes.author: maintainer

repo_notes.content: CONSUMER CONSTRAINTS that any useful page set must convey. The package ships four products, a shape modelled on apple/swift-openapi-generator: PJSIPSwiftGenCore, the library holding header parsing, type discovery and generation; pjsip-swift-gen, a thin CLI over it; PJSIPSwiftGenPlugin, a build-tool plugin that regenerates on every build of the consuming target; and PJSIPSwiftGenCommand, a command plugin that generates on demand and needs writeToPackageDirectory permission because it writes generated Swift back into the package source directory. A consumer chooses either plugin or both. The consumer must declare BOTH swift-pjsip-gen and swift-pjsip as dependencies, because the plugin finds PJSIP's headers by walking the dependency graph for the swift-pjsip checkout. Per-target configuration is a pjsip-swift-gen.json placed in the target's source directory, which for an Xcode app target must be added to the target so the plugin sees it among its input files. The tools require macOS 13 or later. Generated conformances track the exact PJSIP version linked, so bumping swift-pjsip regenerates them rather than leaving hand-written extensions to rot.
